newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM orders police to court in murder case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM orders police to court in murder case.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz on Wednesday ordered dozens of policemen to attend a trial in which they are accused of involvement in the murder of a leftist journalist.

Yilmaz phoned Interior Minister Murat Basesgioglu in the presence of journalists lobbying the prime minister for press freedom and told him to ensure the policemen charged in the case attend the latest hearing in their trial on Thursday.
"Phone the chief of national police and tell him to bring these men to court tomorrow, wherever they are," a journalist present quoted Yilmaz as saying.
The 48 policemen charged with the beating to death of journalist Metin Goktepe have been exempted by court officials from attending any of the hearings in the case.
They face sentences of between three and 15 years.
Goktepe was allegedly beaten to death while in police custody in January, 1996. He was one of scores of people rounded up for an identity check after the funerals of two far-left prisoners.

The case has been delayed after being transferred twice to different provinces for what officials said were security reasons. Human rights activists say the moves were attempts to keep the case out of the public eye by delaying the trial.
Yilmaz's government on Wednesday also took limited steps to relax restrictions on the press.
The government delivered a draft law to the parliamentary speaker's office proposing suspending the trials or sentences for three years in some press cases.
